# Property Transactions

```{r,echo=FALSE,warning=FALSE,message=FALSE}
library(DT)
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)
library(openxlsx)

# Load and clean data
df <- read.xlsx("~/7.Narration/8.Property unit reports/Input/property_transactions_1750066258149.xlsx")
colnames(df) <- make.names(colnames(df))

# Convert TRANSACTION.DATE to Date format
df$TRANSACTION.DATE <- as.Date(df$TRANSACTION.DATE)

# Helper function to format numbers
format_number <- function(x) {
  format(round(x, 2), big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)
}

# Helper function to format currency
format_currency <- function(x) {
  paste0("SAR ", format_number(x))
}

neigh_summary <- df %>%
  group_by(NEIGHBORHOOD) %>%
  summarise(total_value = sum(VALUE..SAR., na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  arrange(desc(total_value))

# Step 2: Get the top neighborhood
highest_neighbourhood <- neigh_summary$NEIGHBORHOOD[1]

# Step 3: Filter transactions for this neighborhood and get the highest individual transaction
highest_trans <- df %>%
  filter(NEIGHBORHOOD == highest_neighbourhood) %>%
  arrange(desc(VALUE..SAR.)) %>%
  slice(1)

# Step 4: Extract formatted fields
highest_date <- format(highest_trans$TRANSACTION.DATE, "%B %d, %Y")
highest_value <- format_currency(df %>%
  filter(NEIGHBORHOOD == highest_neighbourhood) %>%
  summarise(sum(VALUE..SAR.)))
highest_area <- format_number(highest_trans$TRANSACTION.AREA..sqm.)
highest_rate <- format_currency(highest_trans$PROPERTY.TRANSACTION.RATE..SAR.sqm.)

# Step 5: Get the next top 2 neighborhoods (excluding the highest one)
top_zones <- neigh_summary %>%
  filter(NEIGHBORHOOD != highest_neighbourhood) %>%
  slice_head(n = 2) %>%
  pull(NEIGHBORHOOD) %>%
  paste(collapse = " and ")


# 1.2 **Most Active Areas by Transactions by Neighbourhood**
most_active_neighbourhood <- df %>%
  group_by(NEIGHBORHOOD) %>%
  summarise(n_trans = n()) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_trans)) %>%
  slice(1)
most_active_name <- most_active_neighbourhood$NEIGHBORHOOD
most_active_count <- format_number(most_active_neighbourhood$n_trans)

# 1.3 **Most Active Areas by Transactions by Zoning**
zone_summary <- df %>%
  group_by(ZONE) %>%
  summarise(n_trans = n(), total_value = sum(VALUE..SAR., na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_trans))
most_active_zone <- zone_summary$ZONE[1]
most_active_zone_count <- format_number(zone_summary$n_trans[1])
highest_value_zone <- zone_summary %>%
  arrange(desc(total_value)) %>%
  slice(1)
highest_value_zone_name <- highest_value_zone$ZONE
highest_value_zone_count <- format_number(highest_value_zone$n_trans)
highest_value_zone_total <- format_currency(highest_value_zone$total_value)

# 1.5 **High Demand, Low Supply Neighbourhoods**

# Step 1: Aggregate average rate and transaction count by neighborhood
high_demand_raw <- df %>%
  group_by(NEIGHBORHOOD) %>%
  summarise(
    avg_rate = mean(`PROPERTY.TRANSACTION.RATE..SAR.sqm.`, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_trans = n()
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Step 2: Add percentile ranks (normalized)
high_demand_ranked <- high_demand_raw %>%
  mutate(
    rate_rank = percent_rank(avg_rate),
    count_rank = percent_rank(n_trans)
  )

# Step 3: Filter high-rate + low-count neighborhoods
high_demand <- high_demand_ranked %>%
  filter(rate_rank > 0.80, count_rank < 0.40) %>%
  arrange(desc(avg_rate)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 3)

# Step 4: Assign output variables

high_demand_1_count <- high_demand$n_trans[1]

high_demand_2_count <- high_demand$n_trans[2]

# 1.6 **Development Density Ratio (DDR) by Zone**

# Step 1 & 2: Filter and compute DDR
density_df <- df %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(`TRANSACTION.AREA..sqm.`),
    !is.na(`BUILT.UP.AREA..sqm.`),
    !is.na(ZONE)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    DDR = `BUILT.UP.AREA..sqm.` / `TRANSACTION.AREA..sqm.`
  ) %>%
  filter(DDR > 0, DDR <= 2)

# Step 3: Average DDR per zone
ddr_summary <- density_df %>%
  group_by(ZONE) %>%
  summarise(avg_ddr = mean(DDR, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  arrange(desc(avg_ddr))

# Step 4: Output variables (rounded to percent)
ddr_1 <- ddr_summary$ZONE[1]
ddr_1_value <- round(ddr_summary$avg_ddr[1] * 100)

ddr_2 <- ddr_summary$ZONE[2]
ddr_2_value <- round(ddr_summary$avg_ddr[2] * 100)

ddr_3 <- ddr_summary$ZONE[3]
ddr_3_value <- round(ddr_summary$avg_ddr[3] * 100)

ddr_4 <- ddr_summary$ZONE[4]
ddr_4_value <- round(ddr_summary$avg_ddr[4] * 100)

#-------
# Calculate quantiles for price bands (0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%)
# Calculate quantiles for price bands
price_quantiles <- quantile(df$VALUE..SAR., probs = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1), na.rm = TRUE)

# Round quantiles to intuitive boundaries
rounded_quantiles <- c(
  floor(price_quantiles[1] / 100000) * 100000,  # Minimum (likely 0 or close to it)
  round(price_quantiles[2] / 100000) * 100000,  # Round 25th percentile to nearest 100,000
  round(price_quantiles[3] / 100000) * 100000,  # Round 50th percentile to nearest 100,000
  round(price_quantiles[4] / 100000) * 100000,  # Round 75th percentile to nearest 100,000
  ceiling(price_quantiles[5] / 100000) * 100000 # Maximum (rounded up)
)

# Create labels for price bands
band_labels <- c(
  paste0("Under SAR ", format(rounded_quantiles[2], big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)),
  paste0("SAR ", format(rounded_quantiles[2], big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE), "-", 
         format(rounded_quantiles[3], big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)),
  paste0("SAR ", format(rounded_quantiles[3], big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE), "-", 
         format(rounded_quantiles[4], big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)),
  paste0("Greater SAR ", format(rounded_quantiles[4], big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE))
)

# Create price bands and summarize
price_bands <- df %>%
  mutate(
    price_band = case_when(
      VALUE..SAR. < rounded_quantiles[2] ~ band_labels[1],
      VALUE..SAR. >= rounded_quantiles[2] & VALUE..SAR. < rounded_quantiles[3] ~ band_labels[2],
      VALUE..SAR. >= rounded_quantiles[3] & VALUE..SAR. < rounded_quantiles[4] ~ band_labels[3],
      VALUE..SAR. >= rounded_quantiles[4] ~ band_labels[4]
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(price_band) %>%
  summarise(n_trans = n()) %>%
  mutate(
    percentage = n_trans / sum(n_trans) * 100,
    percentage_rounded = round(percentage),  # Round to whole numbers
    price_band = factor(price_band, levels = band_labels)
  ) %>%
  arrange(price_band)

# Adjust percentages to sum to 100
total_pct <- sum(price_bands$percentage_rounded)
if (total_pct != 100) {
  # Calculate the difference
  diff <- 100 - total_pct
  # Find the bucket with the smallest rounding error (closest to the next whole number)
  rounding_errors <- price_bands$percentage - floor(price_bands$percentage)
  max_error_idx <- which.max(rounding_errors)
  price_bands$percentage_rounded[max_error_idx] <- price_bands$percentage_rounded[max_error_idx] + diff
}

# Extract counts and percentages
band_1_count <- format_number(price_bands$n_trans[1])
band_1_pct <- price_bands$percentage_rounded[1]
band_2_count <- format_number(price_bands$n_trans[2])
band_2_pct <- price_bands$percentage_rounded[2]
band_3_count <- format_number(price_bands$n_trans[3])
band_3_pct <- price_bands$percentage_rounded[3]
band_4_count <- format_number(price_bands$n_trans[4])
band_4_pct <- price_bands$percentage_rounded[4]
```

## English Reports {.tabset}

### REPORT-1

#### 1.1. **Highest Transaction in a Neighbourhood**

On **`r highest_date`**, **`r highest_neighbourhood`** recorded the highest investment activity, marked by a significant transaction valued at **`r highest_value`** for a **`r highest_area`** sqm property at a premium rate of **`r highest_rate`** per sqm—indicating strong investor confidence. **`r top_zones`** followed closely in terms of high-value investment zones.

#### 1.2. **Most Active Areas by Transactions by Neighbourhood**

**`r most_active_name`** emerged as the most active neighborhood, recording over **`r most_active_count`** transactions, which underscores its high liquidity and sustained investor interest.

#### 1.3. **Most Active Areas by Transactions by Zoning**

**`r most_active_zone`** lead in transaction volume with **`r most_active_zone_count`** deals, highlighting strong interest in land development and resale, while **`r highest_value_zone_name`**, though lower in count (**`r highest_value_zone_count`** transactions), dominate in value—exceeding **`r highest_value_zone_total`**, reflecting demand for larger or multi-unit assets.

#### 1.4. **Neighbourhoods with the Highest Property Rates (SAR/sqm)**

**`r top_rate_1`** ranks highest nationally with an average property rate of **`r top_rate_1_value`**/sqm, based on **`r top_rate_1_count`** transactions in the Residential Building zone. **`r top_rate_2`** and **`r top_rate_3`** follow closely, averaging **`r top_rate_2_value`** and **`r top_rate_3_value`**/sqm, respectively, from **`r top_rate_2_count`** and **`r top_rate_3_count`** transactions.

#### 1.5. **High Demand, Low Supply Neighbourhoods**

**`r high_demand_1`** leads as a high-demand, low-supply neighbourhood, registering an impressive **`r high_demand_1_rate`**/sqm in **`r high_demand_1_count`** transaction. Following closely are **`r high_demand_2`** and **`r high_demand_3`**, which posted **`r high_demand_2_rate`**/sqm (**`r high_demand_2_count`** transactions) and **`r high_demand_3_rate`**/sqm (**`r high_demand_3_count`** transactions), respectively.

#### 1.6. **Development Density Ratio (DDR) by Zone**

**`r ddr_1`** zones recorded the highest average Development Density Ratio (DDR), with built-up areas occupying **`r ddr_1_value`**% of available land. **`r ddr_2`** followed with **`r ddr_2_value`**%, while **`r ddr_3`** showed a **`r ddr_3_value`**% utilization. **`r ddr_4`** zones had the lowest at just **`r ddr_4_value`**%.

#### 1.7. **Price Band Analysis – Affordability Segmentation**

An affordability-based analysis reveals that the largest share of transactions—over **`r band_1_pct`%**—falls within the **`r band_labels[1]`** segment, accounting for **`r band_1_count`** properties. Properties priced in the **`r band_labels[2]`** range represent **`r band_2_pct`%** of transactions (**`r band_2_count`** units), while those in the **`r band_labels[3]`** range form **`r band_3_pct`%** of the market (**`r band_3_count`** deals). Transactions in the **`r band_labels[4]`** segment contribute **`r band_4_pct`%** to the overall volume, totaling **`r band_4_count`** units.

#### 10.5. **مناطق ذات طلب مرتفع وعرض منخفض**

سجلت **`r high_demand_1`** أعلى معدل سعر بواقع **`r high_demand_1_rate`** ريال/م² من خلال **`r high_demand_1_count`** معاملة، مما يجعلها في مقدمة المناطق ذات الطلب المرتفع والعرض المحدود. تلتها **`r high_demand_2`** و**`r high_demand_3`** بمعدلات **`r high_demand_2_rate`** و**`r high_demand_3_rate`** ريال/م² عبر **`r high_demand_2_count`** و**`r high_demand_3_count`** معاملات على التوالي.

#### 10.6. **نسبة كثافة التطوير حسب المنطقة (DDR)**

يُظهر التحليل المكاني أن مناطق **`r ddr_1`** هي الأعلى من حيث كثافة التطوير بنسبة **`r ddr_1_value`**٪، تليها **`r ddr_2`** بنسبة **`r ddr_2_value`**٪، و**`r ddr_3`** بنسبة **`r ddr_3_value`**٪. بينما سجلت **`r ddr_4`** أدنى نسبة استخدام للأرض عند **`r ddr_4_value`**٪.

#### 10.7. **تحليل نطاقات الأسعار – تقسيم القدرة على الشراء**

تركزت معظم المعاملات (**`r band_1_count`** وحدة، بنسبة تزيد عن **`r band_1_pct`**٪) ضمن نطاق أقل من 500 ألف ريال. وساهم النطاق التالي (500 ألف – 1 مليون ريال) بـ **`r band_2_pct`**٪ من خلال **`r band_2_count`** وحدة، في حين سجلت معاملات النطاق (1 – 2 مليون ريال) نسبة **`r band_3_pct`**٪ (**`r band_3_count`**) وتجاوزت معاملات أكثر من 2 مليون ريال نسبة **`r band_4_pct`**٪ بعدد **`r band_4_count`** صفقة.


### REPORT-11
#### 11.1. **أعلى معاملة في حي**

حدثت المعاملة التي وضعت المعيار في **`r highest_neighbourhood`** بتاريخ **`r highest_date`**، بقيمة **`r highest_value`** لقطعة أرض بمساحة **`r highest_area`** متر مربع، وبسعر **`r highest_rate`** ريال/م². كما كانت أحياء **`r top_zones`** من بين المناطق الرائدة في الاستثمار.

#### 11.2. **المناطق الأكثر نشاطًا حسب المعاملات حسب الحي**

يُعد **`r most_active_name`** الحي الأكثر نشاطًا من حيث عدد المعاملات، بتسجيله أكثر من **`r most_active_count`** صفقة عقارية، ما يعكس حيوية السوق وسرعة حركته.

#### 11.3. **المناطق الأكثر نشاطًا حسب المعاملات حسب التصنيف**

تشير اتجاهات المعاملات إلى أن **`r most_active_zone`** هو التصنيف الأكثر نشاطًا من حيث الحجم، بإجمالي **`r most_active_zone_count`** صفقة، ما يدل على ارتفاع الطلب على الأراضي. في المقابل، ورغم عدد الصفقات الأقل (**`r highest_value_zone_count`**)، حقق **`r highest_value_zone_name`** أعلى قيمة إجمالية تجاوزت **`r highest_value_zone_total`**.

#### 11.4. **الأحياء ذات أعلى معدلات الممتلكات (ريال/م²)**

يتصدر **`r top_rate_1`** قائمة الأحياء من حيث متوسط السعر بواقع **`r top_rate_1_value`** ريال/م² عبر **`r top_rate_1_count`** صفقة. يليه **`r top_rate_2`** بسعر **`r top_rate_2_value`** ريال/م² (**`r top_rate_2_count`** صفقة) ثم **`r top_rate_3`** بسعر **`r top_rate_3_value`** ريال/م² (**`r top_rate_3_count`** صفقة).

#### 11.5. **أحياء الطلب العالي والعرض المحدود**

تتصدر **`r high_demand_1`** المناطق ذات الطلب العالي والعرض المحدود، بمعدل **`r high_demand_1_rate`** ريال/م² من خلال **`r high_demand_1_count`** صفقة. تليها **`r high_demand_2`** بـ **`r high_demand_2_count`** صفقة بسعر **`r high_demand_2_rate`** ريال/م²، ثم **`r high_demand_3`** بـ **`r high_demand_3_count`** صفقة بسعر **`r high_demand_3_rate`** ريال/م².

#### 11.6. **نسبة كثافة التطوير (DDR) حسب المنطقة**

تأتي مناطق **`r ddr_1`** في المقدمة من حيث كثافة التطوير بنسبة **`r ddr_1_value`**٪ من استخدام الأرض، تليها **`r ddr_2`** بنسبة **`r ddr_2_value`**٪ و**`r ddr_3`** بنسبة **`r ddr_3_value`**٪. أما مناطق **`r ddr_4`** فقد سجلت أدنى استخدام للأرض بنسبة **`r ddr_4_value`**٪ فقط.

#### 11.7. **تحليل نطاق الأسعار – تجزئة القدرة الشرائية**

يستمر السكن الميسور في الهيمنة، حيث سُجلت **`r band_1_count`** صفقة لعقارات تقل عن 500 ألف ريال، ما يمثل أكثر من **`r band_1_pct`**٪ من حجم السوق. تليها الفئة من 500 ألف إلى مليون ريال بنسبة **`r band_2_pct`**٪ (**`r band_2_count`** صفقة)، ثم الفئة من مليون إلى مليونين ريال بنسبة **`r band_3_pct`**٪ (**`r band_3_count`** صفقة)، وأخيرًا العقارات فوق مليونين ريال بنسبة **`r band_4_pct`**٪ (**`r band_4_count`** صفقة).

# Unit Transactions
  
```{r,echo=FALSE,warning=FALSE,message=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(scales)
library(openxlsx)
library(lubridate)
library(stringr)
library(DT)
# Load and clean data once
df <- read.xlsx("~/7.Narration/8.Property unit reports/Input/unit_transactions_1750066298503.xlsx")
datatable(
  df,
  options = list(
    pageLength = 10,         
    scrollX = TRUE           
  )
)
df <- read.xlsx("~/7.Narration/8.Property unit reports/Input/unit_transactions_1750066298503.xlsx") %>%
  filter(OUTLIER == "No") %>%
  mutate(
    VALUE = as.numeric(`VALUE.(SAR)`),
    AREA = as.numeric(`UNIT.AREA.(sqm)`),
    RATE = as.numeric(`TRANSACTION.RATE.(SAR/sqm)`),
    DATE = as.Date(`TRANSACTION.DATE`),
    NEIGHBORHOOD = str_to_title(NEIGHBORHOOD),
    ZONE = str_to_title(ZONE)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(VALUE), !is.na(AREA), !is.na(RATE), !is.na(DATE), !is.na(NEIGHBORHOOD), !is.na(ZONE))

#--------------- Point 1: High-Value Transactions
# Get top 2 high-value transactions
top_tx_hv <- df %>% arrange(desc(VALUE)) %>% slice(1:2)

# Format values for sentence
hv_n1 <- top_tx_hv$NEIGHBORHOOD[1]
hv_a1 <- paste0(formatC(top_tx_hv$AREA[1], format = "f", digits = 0), " sqm")
hv_v1 <- dollar(top_tx_hv$VALUE[1], prefix = "SAR ", big.mark = ",", largest_with_cents = Inf)
hv_r1 <- formatC(top_tx_hv$RATE[1], format = "f", digits = 0, big.mark = ",")
hv_d1 <- format(top_tx_hv$DATE[1], "%B %d, %Y")

hv_n2 <- top_tx_hv$NEIGHBORHOOD[2]
hv_a2 <- paste0(formatC(top_tx_hv$AREA[2], format = "f", digits = 0), " sqm")
hv_v2 <- dollar(top_tx_hv$VALUE[2], prefix = "SAR ", big.mark = ",", largest_with_cents = Inf)
hv_r2 <- formatC(top_tx_hv$RATE[2], format = "f", digits = 0, big.mark = ",")
hv_d2 <- format(top_tx_hv$DATE[2], "%B %d, %Y")

#--------------- Point 2: Premium Pricing by Neighborhood
# Average rate per neighborhood
rate_by_neigh_p <- df %>%
  group_by(NEIGHBORHOOD) %>%
  summarise(avg_rate = mean(RATE, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(avg_rate))

# Top 3 premium neighborhoods
top3_p <- rate_by_neigh_p %>% slice(1:3)
# One affordable neighborhood
low1_p <- rate_by_neigh_p %>% slice_tail(n = 1)

# Format values (round to nearest hundred)
p_n1 <- top3_p$NEIGHBORHOOD[1]
p_r1 <- paste0("SAR ", formatC(round(top3_p$avg_rate[1], -2), format = "f", digits = 0, big.mark = ","))
p_n2 <- top3_p$NEIGHBORHOOD[2]
p_r2 <- paste0("SAR ", formatC(round(top3_p$avg_rate[2], -2), format = "f", digits = 0, big.mark = ","))
p_n3 <- top3_p$NEIGHBORHOOD[3]

#--------------- Point 3: High-Demand Neighborhoods

#--------------- Point 4: Property Type Trends
# Function to get zone-level top neighborhood and rate summary (with filtering)
get_zone_summary <- function(zone_name) {
  zone_df <- df %>%
    filter(ZONE == zone_name, !is.na(RATE), !is.na(NEIGHBORHOOD), NEIGHBORHOOD != "UNKNOWN")
  
  if (nrow(zone_df) < 5) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  top_neigh <- zone_df %>%
    group_by(NEIGHBORHOOD) %>%
    summarise(n = n(), avg_rate = mean(RATE, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    arrange(desc(n)) %>%
    slice(1) %>%
    pull(NEIGHBORHOOD)
  
  stats <- zone_df %>%
    filter(NEIGHBORHOOD == top_neigh) %>%
    summarise(
      min_rate = min(RATE, na.rm = TRUE),
      max_rate = max(RATE, na.rm = TRUE),
      avg_rate = mean(RATE, na.rm = TRUE)
    )
  
  if (is.na(stats$min_rate) | is.na(stats$max_rate) | is.na(stats$avg_rate)) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  list(
    neighborhood = top_neigh,
    min_rate = round(stats$min_rate),
    max_rate = round(stats$max_rate),
    avg_rate = round(stats$avg_rate)
  )
}
```
